newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 17.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- LUTON PLAN TO PUT AIRPORT OUT TO FRANCHISE

Luton Borough Council is to seek bids for a franchise of up to 30 years to run Luton Airport. The airport is seeking investment of 170m stg to help fund a new runway and terminal as it seeks to almost triple its passenger volumes. Union Bank of Switzerland, financial advisers to the council, will handle the franchising process.
-- OFEX REBUKE FOR INTERNET COMPANY

Ofex, the junior stock market, has rebuked the Internet software company Display.IT for delaying an announcement about the resignation of a director. The company waited eight days before informing Newstrack, which regulates announcements on Ofex, about the resignation of non-executive director Bill Murphy last week.
-- PLASMON PLUMMETS AFTER LOSS WARNING

Shares in Plasmon, the optical data storage group, fell by 48 per cent to an all-time low of 92.5p on Wednesday following a warning that the group would plunge into the red at the full- year stage. Plasmon said that overall sales had fallen by 4 per cent in the first quarter, and by 16 per cent in Europe, and blamed tough conditions in the CD-Recordable discs market.
THE TIMES
-- BRUSSELS OPPOSES BOEING MERGER

The European Commission is now expected to block the proposed aerospace merger between US groups Boeing and McDonnell Douglas after European Union anti-trust experts came out in opposition to the deal on Wednesday night. A trade war could now ensue after the governments in Bonn, Paris and Washington each expressed support for their respective aerospace industries.
-- CBI URGES BLAIR TO DELAY EURO

Prime minister Tony Blair will be told on Thursday that British employers want the UK to delay joining the single European currency in its early stages. Leaders of the Confederation of British Industry are to tell Blair that although business is broadly in favour of the euro, Britain must wait to see if monetary union is effective before taking part.
-- BT PLEDGES TO PROCEED WITH MCI MERGER

British Telecom, which held its annual meeting on Wednesday, has pledged to complete its proposed 12bn stg merger with MCI despite the announcement of a profits warning by the US firm last week. However, BT chairman Sir Iain Vallance did suggest that the company may renegotiate the price following an extensive review, which will begin immediately.
THE GUARDIAN
-- DRINKS SUPERGROUP BLOCKED

Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, the two UK drinks groups which had planned a 24bn stg mega-merger, have snubbed an offer from French luxury goods firm LVMH to form an alternative, three-way alliance. LVMH, which opposes the two-way merger, is the largest single shareholder in both the UK groups, and the snub means it may now be forced to buy more shares in GrandMet in an effort to block the merger.
-- BANK'S MONETARY COMMITTEE VOTED UNANIMOUSLY FOR JUNE RATE RISE

Minutes of the inaugural meeting of the Bank of England's newly-formed monetary policy committee reveal that the decision to raise interest rates last months was taken unanimously. The six committee members who have been appointed - there will eventually be nine - concurred that a 'modest increase in interest rates was needed immediately'.
-- NATWEST POISED TO TRIM ROLE OF SCANDAL-HIT MARKETS ARM

It has been reported that National Westminster Bank is set to strip out corporate lending and treasury operations from its NatWest Markets investment banking subsidiary in a move aimed at rehabilitating itself in the eyes of discontented shareholders. A review of all operations at NatWest Markets is underway following the disclosure earlier this year of a 90m stg black hole in operations earnings.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- REBEL TENANTS THREATEN INNTREPRENEUR SALE

The planned sale of pub group Inntrepreneur by joint owners Fosters and Grand Metropolitan has been threatened after one third of the company's tenants refused to sign to the new lease which commits them to buying beer from the group. The rebel tenants, over 800 in all, seem intent on taking legal action against Inntrepreneur in a dispute over their existing leases.
-- PEARSON SEEKS BUYER FOR MEDICAL PUBLISHING ARM

Media group Pearson is reported to be looking to dispose of its medical publishing arm, which comprises the Churchill Livingstone and Churchill Communications companies. The disposal would raise about 100m stg, enough to cover the group's losses from the unauthorised discounting scandal at Penguin USA.
-- SETBACK FOR SALE OF FREEMANS

The government has agreed to extend the deadline for the Monopolies & Mergers Commission report on the proposed sale of the Freemans home shopping division to Littlewoods. The decision will come as a blow to troubled retail group Sears, owner of Freemans, which had been hoping that a planned 410m stg pay back to shareholders later this year would be largely funded by the 367.5m stg deal.
